versions.name: Camp Grimes

features.note: Riding program with about 25 miles of trail rides, taught by a certified instructor.
A working forge in the frontier-area blacksmith shop, used for candle-holder and metal craft.
A frontier area with an old log cabin and blacksmith shop interpreting pioneer life.
Trails around the reservation; the camp provides bikes and helmets.
Includes a whitewater kayaking course for older Scouts.
Bass fishing on the lake, with a fishing cabin and an angler award track.
Lake Calhoun, noted for its bass fishing.
Includes leatherwork, candle making, and a woodworking shop.
A climbing and rappelling tower, plus an indoor climbing wall for wet weather.
A dedicated cowboy action range.
Activity fields plus a full-size basketball court.
A large permanent shelter in each of the thirteen campsites.
Two youth shower houses plus a separate adult shower house.
An amphitheatre used for the opening campfire.
Wall tents with two cots each, raised on wooden platforms.
Three campsites have eight-person Adirondacks alongside tents.
A wheelchair-accessible toilet stall; golf-cart access can be approved for mobility needs.
Provisional Scouts are placed with another troop for the week.
Trailblazers, an all-day first-year camper program built on the national model.
An Adventure Academy track of older-Scout award courses.

versions.summary: Mecklenburg County Council's resident summer camp for Scouts BSA, located in Nebo, North Carolina.

provenance.notes: Imported from camp-finder; raw description and sessions dropped (operational data stays at the council site). verified_at is camp-finder's own source-confirmation date; imported_at is when open-scout-api ingested it. The evergreen summary is original prose regenerated from that description, excluding dates/fees/schedules. camp_type classified from program_types. Features surveyed 2026-07-25 against the council's own camp page (that page is explicitly not an exhaustive activity list, so absence of a code is not evidence of absence).
